The incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, leaving the Catholic community distressed over the violation of the sacred worship centre.
An Augustinian priest familiar with the incident told LEADERSHIP that the thieves made away with several items, including fans, regulators, light bulbs, vestments, chalices, ciboriums and other metallic objects.
He said the Tabernacle, where consecrated Hosts are kept, was also vandalised, while the ciborium containing the Blessed Sacrament was taken away.
Explaining the significance of the incident, the priest said, “Destroying the Tabernacle and going away with the consecrated Host is what really constitutes a bigger crime for the Church because that is called desecration. It is no longer theft, but theft and desecration.”
He said the chapel’s sacred objects were among the items taken during the burglary, adding that the removal of the consecrated Hosts made the incident particularly disturbing to the Catholic community.
The priest further explained that the chapel was not a parish but a worship centre established within the Federal Training Centre to serve the spiritual needs of the institution’s students and staff.
The Catholic Archbishop of Kaduna, Most Rev. Matthew Man-Oso Ndagoso, has called on Catholics across the Archdiocese to observe fasting and prayers in reparation for the desecration.
In a statement dated November 17, 2026, addressed to priests, religious and lay faithful, Ndagoso said the incident had left the Catholic community in great distress.
He also announced plans for a Reparation Mass to be celebrated at the chapel, with the date and time to be communicated later.
Christ the King Chapel was established in 1982 and has remained under the pastoral care of priests of the Order of St Augustine (OSA).
